lesson_title: The Envelope That Shrinks: Deductions and the Second Envelope
hook_text: You earned R11 000. You received R8 040. Nobody stole a cent. Here's why.
clip_script: Picture payday as an envelope with your name on it. Inside sits everything you earned this month: eleven thousand rand. But between the shop's safe and your hands, the envelope makes five stops. Stop one, the tax office: one thousand four hundred and thirty out. Stop two, the retirement jar: eight hundred and twenty-five — posted to your own future self. Stop three, the just-in-case insurance: one hundred and ten. Stop four, the doctor cover: five hundred and twenty. Stop five, the union: seventy-five. The envelope arrives holding eight thousand and forty rand. And here is the crucial way to see it: nothing was taken FROM you. Every rand that left was YOUR money, sent ahead to places you agreed it should go.
visual_style: A travelling envelope crossing five glowing checkpoints, a coin counter ticking down from 11 000 to 8 040, each stop stamping its destination on the envelope.
pacing: Steady stop-by-stop rhythm with a warm landing on the final reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and meet the second envelope nobody ever shows you.
